## Body

BLOCK -- #253 at ac8a00daf5c0ca017d4fc858e4a0eee5ae72e913

The named failure responses and the restart-before-bind case improve F211, but binding is still mistaken for a settled spawn answer in two normal cancellation/restart orderings.

R253-001 [P2] Preserve the bind observation until the request is settled.
Location: crates/daemon/src/spawn_waits.rs:78-85; related registration.rs:299-310 and spawn_waits.rs:120-126.

Interleaving: (1) watch(spawn_id) installs Waiting; (2) the child registers, and take_unreported sees Waiting and returns None without recording that it bound; (3) the spawn request is dropped before answering, and Drop changes Waiting to Unreported. The only reporting trigger has already run. No notice or spawn.unreported event follows unless this already-bound seat happens to register again. Claude/Codex binders consider only unbound seats, so their normal tick does not rescue it. The caller has no answer and the parent has no notice, although the seat is running. A model-mismatch spawn can remain bound and unanswered during its existing footer wait, so this is not limited to the success return's tiny synchronous window.

There is a related early-settlement window in http/mod.rs:1893-1898: a bound failure calls watch.answered() before awaiting log IO and failure-event publication. Dropping that request during those awaits has already removed its abandonment guard.

Keep the bound and answer-settlement facts independent, and make either ordering of bind and abandonment complete the handoff once. Add a focused bind-then-drop case, including a bound failure whose response construction is interrupted. The current state test exercises drop-then-take, not this ordering.

R253-002 [P2] Recover bound-but-unanswered launches across restart.
Location: crates/daemon/src/spawn_waits.rs:47-52.

A child can persist its process binding while its spawn handler still waits, before the caller receives an answer. If the daemon restarts there, the caller gets the same transport-level failure that motivated F211, but inherit() excludes the row because proc is Some. Its re-registration therefore finds no Unreported entry and cannot tell the parent. The in-memory guard is lost with the daemon. The same exclusion loses a notice if the detached reporter has consumed the entry but the daemon exits before admitting the send.

Process binding is not evidence that an answer or notice was completed. Recover unsettled launches using evidence of their reporting/settlement, without treating every historical successful bound spawn as a failure. Add a restart-after-bind/before-answer regression. boot_inherits_only_live_unbound_launches currently asserts that every bound row is skipped, and the HTTP restart regression starts with proc None, so neither catches this case.

Requested checks:

- Success ordering: answered() consumes the guard and sets settled, so a later Drop or slow reader does not itself generate a false failure. This does not prove receipt by the client: settlement precedes writing the HTTP response. No local client-drop proof was run.
- Boot/no-wait: the documented --no-wait false-positive notice is real, one per affected inherited launch; bulk spawns can therefore generate several redundant notices. The CLI retries refused connections only, not a reset after a request reached the daemon (crates/cli/src/client.rs:583-609).
- Exactly once: take_unreported removes an entry under its mutex, which suppresses repeat registrations within this daemon; the repeat-registration regression covers that. This is at-most-one reporting attempt, not a restart-safe completed notification, as R253-002 shows.
- Parent gone: no prime fallback exists. Missing/tombstoned parents yield only the spawn.unreported event with withheld="no live parent". A registry read error is also collapsed into that classification by .ok().flatten() at registration.rs:325; the event does not distinguish an unavailable lookup from an absent parent.
- Quoting: neither close-command builder uses pij_core::directory::shell_word (http/mod.rs:1923-1926; registration.rs:320-322). Fresh spawn IDs are grammar-checked and their panes come from tmux, but boot/revive can reuse stored IDs without the fresh-ID check. Reuse the existing helper rather than claiming this is already quoted; no hostile-value close-command test was added. This is a safe-rendering note, not a new same-user authentication requirement.
- Registration wiring: HTTP/identity and both binders share the reporting map. The detached task captures owned clones, not lock guards. The normal prebind path supplies the committed registry parent. The map itself correlates only spawn_id, not the original launch seat/pane/parent; there is no new cross-seat correlation regression.
- Payloads: no env or launch argv is newly copied into the notice. spawn.failed already included captured last_output; this PR does not introduce that existing log surface.
- Policy/cost: this is a notification POLICY, not a destructive brake. No new destructive action is added; the pre-row rollback is unchanged. No new timer, poll, loop rate, or process-launch site is added. Added work is O(N) registry inheritance once per boot, O(1) map work per registration/spawn, and one detached send/event per consumed unreported entry. Existing spawn polling remains 50 ms per waiting spawn. Live before/after cost was not measured by this reviewer.
